title: How to approach a valuation case
description: The first question to ask in a valuation case, how to structure it, and the trap to avoid.
hook: Valuation questions ask what something is worth. You will not need a spreadsheet, just a clear way of thinking about value.
body:
The first question to ask

Valuing a standalone business or a stream of cash flows?

How to build your structure

  • Discounted cash flow (DCF): future cash flows, discounted to today
  • Trading comparables: what similar listed companies are worth, e.g. price to earnings or EV to EBITDA
  • Transaction comparables: what similar companies sold for
  • Use at least two methods and compare

The trap most people fall into

Adding up future years without discounting.

For the full tree, with every branch, read the acquisition (M&A) framework.

Two prompts to try

How would you value a football club for a potential buyer?

Show a model structure
  • Revenue: Media rights, match-day, commercial; Which are contracted vs at risk (relegation)
  • Costs: Player wages and transfers; Stadium, staff; net debt and squad value
  • Value methods: Multiples of recent club deals; Cash-flow value
  • Strategic premium: Brand, stadium, land; What this buyer can add

Where to start: Revenue and how safe it is: media money depends on staying in the league.

The trap: Using one method only; club deals rarely match cash-flow values.
outro: Small things like this add up. Try it in your next practice case and notice how it changes the conversation. Practise this case type in the free casebook: every case has a worked answer.
